issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims (i) that $X$ has finite moments up to order $k$ if and only if $\int_{\|z\|>\epsilon}e^{k\|z\|}\ell(dz)<\infty$, and (ii) that $B_\ell\ge2$ is necessary for the SDE to have a unique solution with finite variance. Both are false. Moment finiteness of $X^{(i)}=X_0^{(i)}e^{rt+L^{(i)}(t)}$ is governed by coordinate-wise exponential moments $\int e^{k z^{(i)}}\ell(dz)$, not by the uniform-norm moment; and an upper bound $\ell=O(e^{-B_\ell\|z\|})$ can never establish necessity. Concrete counterexample from the paper itself: parameter set VG0 ($\alpha=0,\lambda=1,\delta=1,\eta=(-0.1,-0.2)$, $\rho=((0.09,0.06),(0.06,0.16))$) gives $\|\eta\|_\rho^2\approx0.26$, hence $B_\ell=\sqrt{\|\eta\|_\rho^2+2\lambda}-\|\eta\|_\rho\approx0.99<2$, yet this NTS/VG model has an explicit unique solution with finite second moments (e.g. $\lambda-2\eta^{(1)}-2\rho_{11}=1.02>0$ gives $\mathbb{E}[e^{2L^{(1)}(1)}]<\infty$). Thus the paper's standing assumption (2.4) with $B_\ell>2$ excludes its own VG0 test case, while the claim that VG 'satisfies the conditions' is false.

failure_location.quote:
Following \citet[Chapter 6]{applebaum2004}, the stronger condition $B_{\ell}\geq2$ is necessary to guarantee the
existence of a unique solution with finite variance to the stochastic
differential equation (\ref{eq: intro - asset prices dynamics}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false necessity claim by the correct statement (well-posedness and finite variance follow from integrability conditions such as coordinate-wise exponential moments) and weaken the $B_\ell>2$ requirement in (2.4) to what the scheme actually uses (finitely many finite moments plus exponential decay of the tail), or explicitly note that VG0 lies outside the stated hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's stated modelling hypothesis (2.4) with $B_\ell>2$, and the prose supporting it, are internally inconsistent with the VG0 experiment used throughout Section 4; the assumption as stated excludes a model the paper itself prices. The numerical scheme and all reported results are unaffected.
issues.title: False necessity claims on the decay constant B_ell exclude the paper's own VG0 test case
issues.why_classification: A local correction of two supporting prose claims and a weakening of one hypothesis clause; the method, the quadrature, and all experimental guarantees are unaffected, so no new proof architecture or loss of content is involved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The number $A_{\ell}$ governs the activity and variation of the process:

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that for a singular Lévy measure 'it is not possible to apply classical quadrature formulae' and that 'the error will blow up as the number of quadrature points increases'. Under the paper's own assumptions the integrand behaves like $\tfrac12 z^\top H(z)z\,\ell(z)\sim\|z\|^{-A_\ell}$ near the origin with $A_\ell<2$, which is integrable; the composite midpoint/trapezoidal error for such an integrable singularity converges to zero at the reduced rate $O(h_z^{2-A_\ell})$ (inherited by the PIDE solution error). The claimed blow-up is false: classical quadrature converges, just at a deteriorated order. What is true is only the (correct) statement that second order is not obtained.

failure_location.quote:
When the L{\'e}vy measure is singular, it is not possible to apply classical
quadrature formulae, such as the midpoint or the trapezoidal rule.
In fact, in this case the error will blow up as the number of quadrature
points increases.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'the error will blow up as the number of quadrature points increases' by the correct statement that the classical rules converge only at the reduced order $O(h_z^{2-A_\ell})$ and hence do not deliver second-order convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The motivational claim about classical quadrature is mathematically wrong; the motivation for the tailored quadrature is overstated, but the proposed scheme, its derivation, and the reported convergence results are unaffected.
issues.title: Classical quadrature errors do not blow up for singular Lévy measures
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one supporting prose sentence; the numerical method, its derivation, and all advertised guarantees are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Table \ref{tab: test - Variance of the parameters sets}

issues.failure_explanation: By subordination, $\mathbb{V}[L(t)]=\rho\,\mathbb{E}[G(t)]+\eta\eta^\top\mathbb{V}[G(t)]$ with $\mathbb{E}[G(1)]=\delta\Gamma(1-\alpha)/\lambda^{1-\alpha}$ and $\mathbb{V}[G(1)]=\delta\Gamma(2-\alpha)/\lambda^{2-\alpha}$, giving a $\rho$-coefficient $\rho\,\lambda/(1-\alpha)$, not $\rho\,\lambda^{1-\alpha}$. The main-text formula therefore contradicts the paper's own Appendix (Table 4) and its consequences: for NIG0 ($\alpha=1/2$, $\lambda=20766.4$) the main-text formula yields $\sqrt{\mathbb{V}[L^{(1)}(1)]}\approx0.021$, whereas Table 2 reports $0.1958$, which matches the appendix formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term $\rho\lambda^{1-\alpha}$ in the main-text variance display by $\rho\frac{\lambda}{1-\alpha}$ (as in Appendix A, Table 4).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed variance formula for the NTS model in Section 4 is false; it disagrees with the correct formula in the appendix and with the paper's own Table 2. No other result uses this formula.
issues.title: Main-text NTS variance formula is false
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of a peripheral displayed formula; it is not a pure typo because the correct coefficient must be derived or taken from the appendix, but no downstream claim depends on it.
